flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk with Playwright at 1440x900 (DSF 1) and 390x844 (DSF 3). The primary action is 'Book a 15-minute setup call': in the first screen at 1440 it appears as the header a.btn.head-cta and the hero a.btn in .hero-actions, both href='#setup-call'; the repeat is a.btn inside .book in section#setup-call, also href='#setup-call'. No click handlers are attached to any of them (the only listeners are on the demo step buttons and #replay). At 1440, clicking the hero button only scrolls to #setup-call (scrollY 4136); nothing before the click says booking is unavailable (the hero line reads 'A working session, not a pitch: we load your waitlist with you and send a test text to your phone.'). Clicking the card's 'Book a 15-minute setup call' then does nothing: scrollY 4136 before and after, URL still ...index.html#setup-call, no dialog, no new page, no console error. Same at 390: hero click lands at scrollY 6822, card button click leaves scrollY 6822 and URL unchanged; at 390 the card button and its note are below the fold after the hero jump (button top 1028px in an 844px viewport). The only disclosure is the muted line placed under the dead button: 'Our calendar link is being connected. Until it is live, this page cannot take a booking; the agenda on the left is what the call covers.' It does not say what the button does, and the header/hero repeats carry no disclosure at all before the visitor clicks. So the primary action labelled as booking a call scrolls the page to a card whose same-labelled button does nothing - it names a destination (a booking) it does not reach and the repeat does nothing, which the table counts. The 'local action whose real result is stated before the visitor commits' exemption does not apply: there is no local result, just an inert self-anchor, and the brief supplied no booking destination.
